scope: Read-only investigation of the one high npm audit warning from Guro release run 38338220101. No dependency updates, remote writes, audit suppression, security changes, or redeployment.
conclusion: The flagged dependency is present in the locked build toolchain. The audited static release does not ship it or expose its cache-reuse API on public request paths; no current public runtime exposure from this advisory was identified. Keep a scoped dependency-maintenance finding open; this is not a blanket security certification.

readOnlyAudit.workingDirectory: isolated copy of the exact package.json and package-lock.json; no node_modules
readOnlyAudit.exitMeaning: Vulnerability finding, not audit execution failure

upstreamSourcesOpened.observed: Reviewed high advisory, affected <=4.2.0, patched versions listed as None; CVSS 4 page score 8.7 differs from npm CVSS 3.1 score.
Maintainer disputed the report and closed it as not planned on 2026-10-04.
Open request to reconsider the advisory; no settled resolution observed.
Open unmerged change to cache reuse/revalidation behavior, not an established deployed fix.
Tagged original asset-build source consulted alongside installed code.

assessment.runtime: The particular advisory needs a shared cache reuse path accepting client max-stale. This release has no application executable and does not deploy this npm package; the required path was not found.
assessment.build: Astro is a production-classified dependency in package-lock, but its dependency is only part of the build toolchain for this static deployment. The inspected use computes remote-image storage/TTL and does not call the advisory cache-reuse API; this project does not use that image pipeline.
assessment.releaseImpact: No evidence supports emergency rollback or changing the independently verified static release for this finding alone.
assessment.safeNextStep: Retain the warning and original lock. Evaluate a narrowly scoped dependency maintenance change separately using official npm upstream provenance, code diff and clean npm ci/audit, then rerun the full source-contract, test/build and byte/visual review gates before any release. Reassess immediately before adding SSR, server endpoints, authenticated/shared response caching, or remote-image features.
assessment.versionCaveat: npm fixAvailable and 4.3.0 falling outside the advisory range do not by themselves prove a security remediation. The advisory still says no patched version and the upstream dispute is unresolved.

notVerified: No exploit reproduction or full penetration test performed.
No claim about Cloudflare platform internals or unrelated dependencies.
No dependency update was tested or applied.
auditExecutionCaveat: Initial audits without an explicitly writable npm cache produced one advisory plus an Astro metavulnerability and fixAvailable:false. The later successful isolated cached audit is authoritative for this report and reproduces the CI high 1 result. An npm view attempt failed with local cache ENOENT, then succeeded with a writable cache; no access denial was bypassed.
